platform.target_board: STM32F4 Discovery (STM32F407VG) — same core, 1 MB flash / 192 KB RAM
platform.icount: shift=0 (virtual clock advances 1 ns per guest instruction)
platform.timing_semantics: QEMU: deterministic guest instruction counts. Hardware: true CPU cycles. cycles ≈ insns only under IPC=1 for in-order Cortex-M4.
platform.dwt_status: NOT emulated by QEMU for this machine (CYCCNT frozen; probed and confirmed) — hence SysTick

provenance.vendoring: src/vendor/ — verbatim sources, deltas limited to import paths (std::ops->core::ops, alloc::vec), libm for std-gated f64 math (exp/ln/atan2/round), and removal of OS-entropy nonce generation
provenance.crypto_versions: pinned to core_v2/Cargo.lock: aes 0.8.4, aes-gcm 0.10.3, hkdf 0.12.4, hmac 0.12.1, sha2 0.10.9, zeroize 1.9.0 (std features off)

correctness_gates.aes256gcm_1024B_roundtrip: PASS (ciphertext len + tag verify + decrypt match)

determinism: bench/ratio lines byte-identical across independent QEMU runs (icount)

results.units: tck = SysTick ticks = guest instructions under QEMU -icount shift=0

lyapunov_benettin.note: timed over a 100-step run at a distinct IC so LLVM cannot CSE it against the untimed full run; lambda_1 sanity ~0.198 nats/s at 2000 steps (design-stage 0.405 is a longer-horizon value)

aes256gcm_enc_1024B.note: software AES (no HW accelerator on STM32F4); includes per-call key schedule, matching core_v2 AesGcmCipher API

packet_total.composition: HKDF derive + AES-256-GCM encrypt(1024B) + HMAC-SHA256 over 1040B ct

interpretation.epoch_overhead: One epoch of Q32.32 RK4 key-schedule maintenance costs ~10.9 G ticks (~65 s at 168 MHz IPC=1), i.e. ~5.4% of the 1200 s epoch wall-clock — and is the same work the desktop pipeline performs, so no additional per-packet key-derivation burden exists beyond the 53.4k-tick packet path.
interpretation.per_packet_cost: 53.4k ticks/pkt ≈ 318 us at 168 MHz IPC=1 for the full derive+encrypt+commit chain on a 1024 B payload.
interpretation.hardware_pending: These are QEMU-icount instruction counts. A real STM32F4 Discovery run with DWT CYCCNT will measure true cycles (expect higher than IPC=1 due to flash wait states and multi-cycle instructions). The firmware is flash-ready; only the on-hardware capture remains.

firmware.run_hardware: arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary target/thumbv7em-none-eabihf/release/stm32f4-bench bench.bin && st-flash write bench.bin 0x08000000  # semihosting console via openocd or SWO
